newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Swiss Glencore in deal with top Argentine crusher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Glencore in deal with top Argentine crusher.

text.p: Swiss grain traders Glencore have signed an agreement for an option to purchase 51 percent of major Argentine oilseed crusher Oleaginosa Moreno SA, officials from both firms said Wednesday.

"We are interested in the operation, we are interested in (Moreno owner) Mr. Moreno as a partner, and we believe the agreement will be mutually beneficial," Sergio Gancberg, president of Glencore's Argentine operation, told Reuters.
The option agreement is for 150 days, and Gancberg said the price was confidential. Moreno, the world's largest sunflower seed crusher, has annual turnover of $1 billion.

A source close to Moreno said the deal was accelerated by financial problems linked to the company's high levels of debt, but that they hoped Glencore's backing would remove any doubts over the privately-owned firm in the market.

"Moreno is an absolutely viable company and obviously the presence of Glencore makes it even more so," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. "I imagine the firm's competitors are pretty nervous now."

If the purchase goes ahead it will give Glencore its first crushing capacity in Argentina, but the firm would first assess its new buy before deciding whether to invest in any possible expansion, Gancberg said.
Moreno mainly crushes sunflower seed at plants in the southern Buenos Aires province. It also trades wheat.
The deal comes at a time of fast growth in Argentina's crushing industry.

Argentina's crushing capacity has grown to 19.6 million tonnes a year in 1996 from 13.7 million tonnes a year in 1990 and just 4.3 million tonnes in 1980, according to the Argentine Vegetable Oil Industry Chamber (CIARA).

Bigger harvests of soybeans and sunflower seed have helped feed this expansion, which is still continuing. Crushers also see Argentina as a natural low cost producer at a time of expanding world demand for oils and meals.

"Output now is about 60,000 tonnes a day. This year another 5,000 to 7,000 tonnes of daily capacity will probably be added, and then an additional 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes for the next two years," CIARA manager Alberto Rodriguez told Reuters.
U.S. grains giant Cargill recently expanded its Argentine oilseed crushing capacity to 10,000 tonnes a day.
